name: create-application-type-and-mapping-set
description: The tenth layer authored with no new tool and no new address form. One `create` declares the physical view of a signal — its unit, its linear conversion and its range — and a second declares the set that says which implementation type stores it. The `mapping_sets` layer arrived with contract `7.0.0` and has never had an MCP tool of its own; the generic change set reaches it because the registry is derived from the contract, which is the property `create-data-type-alias` was the mandatory vector for.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model, whose `implementation_types` layer (`data_types/implementation/`) holds the value type `float32` and whose `data_types/mapping_sets/` directory is present and empty — the state a project with no physical type is in, and the reason the layer declares `optional: false` and still may hold no file. Neither element the change set creates exists.

authorization.notes: Two element addresses in two layers, one of which had no tool to be named after. Scope is keyed by operation and address throughout, so a layer added by a contract bump needs no scope vocabulary of its own.

input.intent: Declare the physical view of the vehicle speed signal and the set that stores it.

value.name: PhysicalMapping
value.description: Physical types and the implementation types that store them

after.name: PhysicalMapping
after.description: Physical types and the implementation types that store them

expected.notes: `conversion` and `range` are **nested member kinds**, not maps: the contract declares `kind:application_types.conversion` with `factor` and `offset` and `kind:application_types.range` with `min` and `max`, so the payload's keys are checked and a third one is refused — which a `map[string, number]` could not have done. Both are optional and both are omitted on disk at their default, so a type declaring none of the three round-trips byte-identically; `conversion: {}` would be the **identity** conversion and therefore a declaration, where a blank `unit` is no unit. The set's own `maps` is a collection identified by `application` rather than by a `name`, which is why a pair is addressed by the application type it maps. Nothing here checks that the pair's two sides name types of the kinds each side admits, or that a component's ports are covered: those are `mapping-set.unknown-application`, `.unknown-implementation` and `data-type.application-type-unmapped`, and all three are pass D's — `negative/consistency-violation-application-type-unmapped.json` is the last one's refusal. No port in this model speaks the new type yet, so the staged result is consistent.
